purpose: Enable a fictional regional-grid steering committee to approve a staged 2030 modernization portfolio by showing, through an illustrative planning scenario, why visibility, flexibility, and resilience investments must be sequenced together.

screens.purpose: Orient the committee to the Grid Forward 2030 decision and fictional planning context.
State the staged portfolio approval requested and the conditions attached to it.
Make the illustrative demand and reliability gap visible without presenting scenario figures as forecasts.
Explain how visibility, flexibility, and resilience work as three linked modernization priorities.
Compare portfolio choices and identify the staged balanced portfolio as the recommended option.
Show the phase sequence, dependencies, decision gates, and intended progression through 2030.
Connect principal delivery risks to mitigations, owners, and gate conditions.
Request approval and make immediate next actions and accountability explicit.

actions.label: Inspect the illustrative demand and reliability gap
Align on visibility, flexibility, and resilience
Review the phased roadmap and gates
Request approval for the staged portfolio
Approve the staged portfolio subject to phase gates
Defer approval and request additional analysis

constraints: Use exactly eight slides in this order: title, decision, gap, priorities, portfolio, roadmap, risks, approval.
Label every figure and quantitative callout Illustrative planning scenario — not a forecast.
Treat all organizations, portfolio data, metrics, dates, and outcomes as fictional scenario content rather than external facts.
Use a Swiss/data-driven visual system grounded in the steering-committee decision workflow, not in bundled character compositions.
Use the Fantasy Mouse only as a restrained presenter and preserve canonical identity and mutually exclusive default/action hand modes.
Keep the deck editable, accessible, legible at presentation scale, and structured as one clear composition per slide.
Require explicit phase gates, owners, mitigations, and next actions before the approval state.
Do not claim generated, tested, run, rendered, visually checked, compared, or accepted status without corresponding evidence.
